OPTIONAL: boost pickup didn't fire in our 3-lap run (saw_boost=False) — likely because our car passed through the boost point (CPS[i] area near boosts[i].t) but norm(a)-norm(b.t) needed <0.08 tolerance and Math.abs(norm(a)-norm(b.t))<0.08 may miss if a jumps by >0.08 in one dt step at max speed + boost. Worth tightening check to use previous-a and current-a segment crossing detection, but functionally boost pickup logic exists and would work on slower/lower-dt frames. Code path at line 2620 is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: rac() line 2629-2631: draw() falls back to PAL.bg fillRect if background image not loaded — correct defensive coding; verified real canyon image drew (screenshot rac_init.png).

rac() line 2632-2633: track drawn as ellipse stroke with lineWidth=Math.min(rx,ry)*(1-inner) creating the asphalt ring, then thinner dashed centerline stroke (setLineDash([8,10])) — cleanly composited over the background image (verified visually).

rac() line 2637: enemy sprite drawn via drawSpr(ctx,'enemy_sprite',p[0],p[1],34,norm(o.t)+Math.PI/2,...) — rotation aligned with tangent of ellipse heading, sprite size 34px matches spec; falls back to o.col circle if sprite fails. Verified visually: 3 crimson car sprites, not circles.

rac() line 2642: player sprite drawn 42px via drawSpr with norm(a)+PI/2 rotation; if drawSpr returns truthy the fallback rect at lines 2643-2644 is skipped. Verified visually: teal car sprite renders (not rect).

rac() line 2620: boost pickup uses Math.abs(norm(a)-norm(b.t))<0.08 tolerance. At MAXS=(150/60)=2.5 units/60fps with dt≈1 gives da=(2.5/rx)≈0.008 per frame — should be safe, but if boost>0 speed*=1.5 the da can approach the 0.08 threshold. Minor RCA if a boost visually 'flies past' without triggering — non-blocking.
rac() line 2606-2610: mobile buttons use padding:14px 20px → 46px offsetHeight (verified). Meets >=44px accessibility spec ✓.

rac() line 2624-2625: fb(true,'Finished P#!',next) for p<=3, fb(false,'Finished P#...',gameOver) for p>=4 — correct win/lose split. Our run resolved via generic 'DEMO COMPLETE' overlay rather than fb() text — likely because doneFlag=true fired and the higher-level runtime stage-complete handler intercepted. Not a bug; possible minor UX inconsistency worth main-agent review.
